target.title: Instrument native hook relay fan-out
target.body:
## Summary
- add per-registration native hook relay metrics for command requests and real invocations
- log aggregate relay summaries at unregister with event counts, total/max duration, and no-local-work command requests
- warn on slow native hook relay invocations (>=250ms) with relay/session/tool context

## What Problem This Solves
Operators observed short, high-CPU bursts from `openclaw-hooks` workers during normal Telegram/Codex activity. Source inspection points at Codex native hook relay fan-out as a likely hot path: the Codex harness can register native events such as `pre_tool_use`, `post_tool_use`, `permission_request`, and `before_agent_finalize`; when local work exists, those events cross a process boundary through `openclaw hooks relay`.

The important next step is observability, not behavior change. This PR adds low-noise aggregate metrics around the native hook relay path so operators can confirm which relay events are requested, which ones actually invoke OpenClaw work, how long they take, and whether no-local-work requests are still contributing to fan-out.

This PR does not change relay behavior, approval semantics, hook policy, or gateway configuration.

## Evidence
Redacted live host observations from the OpenClaw hook-burst investigation:

- 2026-07-06 hook-cost audit: short-lived `openclaw-hooks` workers were observed around 145-175% CPU during normal Telegram/OpenClaw use, with CPU temperature near 97C in one snapshot. A later audit snapshot reproduced one `openclaw-hooks` worker around 159% CPU while CPU temperature was 83.6C.
- Controlled local timing sample after a temporary operator-only runtime timing patch on OpenClaw 2026.6.11: 19 native relay invocations in roughly 40 seconds, including 10 `pre_tool_use` calls at 1-54ms and 9 `post_tool_use` calls at 0-1ms. No `>=250ms` slow relay lines appeared in that short sample, which suggests the burst problem is likely process fan-out/overlap rather than one slow handler.
- During that same sample, a short-lived `openclaw-hooks` worker was observed around 163% CPU and disappeared within seconds.
- 2026-07-06 post-restart memory watch: pre-restart gateway cgroup memory was about 2.5GB, gateway node RSS about 887MB, swap effectively full, and another short-lived `openclaw-hooks` burst hit about 166% CPU. Immediately after restart, another short-lived hook worker hit about 157% CPU during the first post-restart turn.
- 2026-07-06 workload checkpoint after starting a real Symphony/Codex review lane: gateway cgroup memory rose to about 7.0GB with 584 tasks while gateway node RSS stayed under about 1GB; two short-lived `openclaw-hooks` workers were observed around 162-163% CPU, with multiple Codex app-server workers active under the gateway cgroup. This points at child-process fan-out/worker overlap rather than a single gateway heap-only leak.
- 2026-07-08 follow-up inspection: gateway cgroup memory was about 5.6GB, cgroup peak about 9.1GB, 417 tasks, swap about 7.3GB/8GB used, 8 resident Codex app-server wrapper/native pairs, and a short-lived `openclaw-hooks` worker around 170% CPU / 340MB RSS while inspecting.

Source-level findings from the same investigation:

- The live config did not explicitly set `nativeHookRelay`; the Codex harness enabled native hook relay by default.
- `post_tool_use` and `before_agent_finalize` are locally gated by whether matching global hooks exist, but once local work exists, the relay still crosses a process boundary.
- The generic void-hook path runs matching hook work in parallel, so several short-lived relay processes can overlap during tool-heavy turns.

## Relation To #101099
#101099 was an earlier timing-instrumentation lane from the same investigation. This PR is the cleaner/narrower aggregate-metrics lane:

- #101099 focused on timing logs from an operator patch direction.
- #102241 adds source-level per-registration counters, no-local-work request counts, aggregate unregister summaries, and slow-invocation warnings in one relay file.

If maintainers prefer one observability shape, this PR should supersede or narrow #101099 rather than both landing independently.

## Verification
- `pnpm tsgo:core:test`
- `node scripts/test-projects.mjs extensions/codex/src/app-server/native-hook-relay.test.ts` (13/13)
- `TMPDIR=$(mktemp -d /tmp/openclaw-native-relay-test-XXXXXX) node scripts/test-projects.mjs src/agents/harness/native-hook-relay.test.ts` (80/80)

Note: the same relay test without isolated `TMPDIR` can see a live gateway native-hook bridge record in the shared OS temp dir and fail its PID-isolation expectation; isolating `TMPDIR` avoids that host-local interference.
